about.title: Madera Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice claims are different from ordinary injury cases, and Madera County families dealing with a bad medical outcome often aren't sure where to turn. Whether the harm happened at a local clinic, a Madera hospital, or during a referral to a larger facility, California law (MICRA) sets specific rules for these claims: strict notice requirements, filing deadlines, and a near-universal need for a qualified medical expert to weigh in on what went wrong. A poor result alone doesn't establish fault — the law requires showing the provider fell below the accepted standard of care. LawProactive doesn't practice law or decide your case; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review the medical records and explain what options may exist. If they take your case, they work on contingency, so there's no fee unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Early

items.title: Strict Filing Windows
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from discovering the harm, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to file a malpractice claim. Missing this window can end a valid claim before it starts.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' advance notice of your intent to sue. An attorney can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Usually Required
items.desc: Because a bad outcome alone isn't proof of malpractice, these cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. Getting a case evaluated early gives more time to gather that review.

items.question: Does a bad result from surgery automatically mean malpractice happened in Madera?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that medicine involves risk, and a poor outcome by itself doesn't prove negligence. A claim generally requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard, which is why expert review is so important.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim after treatment at a Madera facility?
items.answer: Generally, California's MICRA rules allow one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a required 90-day notice period before filing suit, so it's worth speaking with an attorney well before any deadline approaches.

items.question: Is there a limit on what I can recover for pain and suffering?
items.answer: Yes, California caps non-economic damages (like pain and suffering) in malpractice cases, though that cap rises each year under current law. Economic damages, such as medical bills and lost income, are generally not subject to that same cap.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to help me find an attorney in Madera?
items.answer: No, connecting you with an independent attorney is free. If an attorney in our network takes your case, they typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
